originality.rationale: Compared statements and implications. Shee arXiv:2409.06920v1/v2 gives the joint-reset harmonic ABP model, the mean-optimal reset rate and exact component second moments (v1 Eq. 9, Eq. 60 and Eq. 63); these basic formulae are established prior art and are not claimed. Both primary HTML manuscripts were examined in the model, second-moment, and phase-diagram sections. Neither explicitly classifies the centered longitudinal-versus-transverse covariance eigenvalue sign for every confinement strength or proves exactly two simple phase boundaries straddling the known mean optimum with the stated endpoint asymptotics. The global two-crossing assertion requires additional quartic factorization and Descartes root-count plus singular-limit analysis; it is not a trivial numerical substitution or same-parameter special case. Baouche et al., arXiv:2405.06769v1, reset orientation but not position; Kumar–Sadekar–Basu arXiv:2008.03294 study unconfined resetting. Broad implicit deduction from the source moment formulas remains a substantial residual priority risk; a semantic search is not proof of uniqueness.

value.rationale: The stationary covariance ellipse is the natural second-order Gaussian-approximation geometry of a driven particle; it controls the directions of typical centered fluctuations. Raw longitudinal second moments are always larger, whereas covariance eigenvalue ordering has two universal strict reversals. The known mean-displacement-optimal resetting rate is always in the transverse-dominant interval for all positive trap strengths. Two exact boundary laws quantify the strength-scale crossover, furnishing a motivated phase classification not captured by existing source kurtosis diagrams; no extension to other resetting mechanisms is claimed.
